taxonomy.subtopic: Postinflammatory ciliary dysfunction with ampullary embryo retention

questions.stem_html: A 29-year-old woman has 6 weeks of amenorrhea, unilateral pelvic pain and light vaginal bleeding. She previously had pelvic inflammatory disease. Serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin is 2,900 mIU/mL; transvaginal ultrasonography shows an empty uterine cavity and a small right adnexal gestational sac. The accompanying diagram marks the segments of the uterine tube. Which mechanism most likely led to implantation at the usual site of this disorder?

options.text_html: Scarring and ciliary dysfunction delayed embryo transport through the ampulla
Failure of Müllerian duct fusion created a blind-ending uterine horn
Premature zona pellucida loss caused implantation on the ovarian surface in most cases
Excess progesterone accelerated smooth-muscle transport into the uterine cavity
Anti-Müllerian hormone caused regression of the ipsilateral uterine tube

questions.explanation_html: Most ectopic pregnancies are tubal, and the ampulla is the most common location. Prior salpingitis can damage the tubal mucosa, impair ciliary activity and distort smooth-muscle transport, allowing the embryo to remain in the tube long enough to implant. An hCG concentration above the local ultrasound discriminatory range without an intrauterine gestational sac increases concern, but definitive diagnosis integrates symptoms, serial hCG and imaging.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: A Müllerian fusion defect can create uterine anomalies, but it does not explain the usual ampullary location after pelvic inflammatory disease.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Ovarian ectopic pregnancy is rare; most ectopic pregnancies are located in the uterine tube.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Progesterone does not accelerate transport into the uterus in this scenario; damaged tubal transport predisposes to retention.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Anti-Müllerian hormone is relevant to fetal Müllerian regression in 46,XY development, not acquired unilateral tubal disease in an adult.

questions.educational_objective: Pelvic inflammatory disease can scar the uterine tube and impair ciliary transport, predisposing to embryo retention and implantation in the ampulla, the most common ectopic site.
